candidate_status: isolated experimental candidate; no live adoption
failure_split: Before six SendBuffer/ForwardBuffer caller-isolation roots fail each3 (18); three optional ACK retention/coverage/retry roots fail each3 (9). Other controls pass before and after.
fixture_correction: Only v2 test setup changed: provider child context before workers, and send-worker hook set in ClientSettings before NewClient. Production bytes match v2 on each side.
hard_contract: Cancellation of an unadmitted caller cannot retire a healthy shared send/forward sequence or reclaim accepted sibling bytes. A genuinely closed sequence still recreates for a live caller.
optional_policy: Existing dedicated pure-ACK worker may retain one control until admission or exact flow/provider/source cancellation. This avoids artificial control loss; loss of a pure ACK remains legal TCP recovery behavior. Exact old+latest replay is not required; latest-only coalescing is valid.
physical_rig_limit: Existing physical A/B/A rejects all provider ReturnSend refusal, including recoverable pure ACKs. That gate can exclude a legal well-performing TCP recovery path; original fixture remains unchanged and results must separate this preference from delivered throughput and byte correctness.
policy_limits: Shared/public/orphan callback refusal stays zero-wait. No queue, byte limit or worker count is increased. No-pressure admission creates no combined context; a context join is created only after actual initial refusal. Accepted control keeps ordinary Transfer ACK timeout.
retention: Original sources, binaries, logs, commands and local paths remain immutable outside Git, represented by hashes.
